rows.title: Illicit stills on Lismore
rows.evidence: The Lismore, Scotland article says that after the 1707 union, taxes on whisky distillation rose and much distillation was forced underground until the 1823 Excise Act, and that the remains of at least two illicit stills from this period have been found on Lismore.
rows.summary: After the union of 1707, taxes on whisky distillation rose dramatically, and much of Scotland's distillation was shut down or forced underground until the 1823 Excise Act. The remains of at least two illicit stills from that period have been found on Lismore. The stills are on the island, from the years when legal whisky distilling had been driven underground.

rows.title: Distilling banned on Tiree
rows.evidence: The Tiree article says the island has a rich distilling history, that distilling was banned in 1802, and that the present company is the first legal distillery on Tiree in over 200 years, set up to re-establish the island's whisky heritage.
rows.reject_reason: The Tiree article says distilling was banned in 1802 and that a company on the island now makes whisky. It does not place illicit stills, a wreck, a film, a novel, or a festival there. The working Isle of Tiree distillery is already filed. The photograph is Balephuil Bay, not a still.
rows.summary: Tiree has a rich distilling history. Distilling on the island was banned in 1802, and the present company is said to be the first legal distillery there in over 200 years. It was set up to re-establish the island's whisky heritage.

rows.title: Old Jura distillery
rows.evidence: The Jura, Scotland article says Jura distillery was founded in 1810, was not used after 1900, and was dismantled, and that in 1963 the old property was taken over and a modern distillery was built. The working Jura distillery is already filed separately. This row is the dismantled 1810 still.
rows.reject_reason: The 1810 distillery was on Jura and was dismantled, but the summary names the estate owners Robin Fletcher of Ardlussa and Tony Riley-Smith of Ardfin. The photograph is a view of houses at Craighouse and the Paps, and its caption does not identify the still.
rows.summary: Jura distillery was founded on Jura in 1810. It was not used after 1900 and was dismantled. In 1963 Robin Fletcher of Ardlussa and Tony Riley-Smith of Ardfin took over the old property and built a modern distillery. The 1810 still is the one that was taken down.

rows.title: The Brothers (1947 film)
rows.evidence: The Brothers (1947 film) article says the unit moved to the Isle of Skye to film, and that the film depicts illicit whisky manufacturing, including an informer who reported illicit whisky trafficking. The plot section says the story is set in the Western Isles and does not use the name Skye for the setting.
rows.reject_reason: The article sets the plot in the Western Isles and places only the location shoot on Skye. It does not put the illicit-whisky story on Skye. The photograph is Blaven from near Torrin, which the article does not tie to the film.
rows.summary: The Brothers is a 1947 film, adapted from L. A. G. Strong's novel, whose plot is set in the Western Isles of Scotland. The unit moved to the Isle of Skye to film it. The film depicts illicit whisky manufacturing, and an informer who has reported illicit whisky trafficking.

rows.title: SS Politician at Calvay
rows.evidence: The Calvay article says it was often quoted that SS Politician ran aground at Calvay with a cargo of whisky, and then says this is untrue and that the ship ran aground on Eriskay.
rows.reject_reason: The Calvay article says the claim that SS Politician ran aground at Calvay with a cargo of whisky is untrue. The ship ran aground on Eriskay, which is already filed.
rows.summary: It was often quoted that SS Politician ran aground at Calvay with a cargo of whisky in 1941 and inspired Compton Mackenzie's novel Whisky Galore. The same article says this is untrue, and that the ship ran aground on Eriskay.

rows.title: Pràban na Linne
rows.evidence: The Isleornsay article says Pràban na Linne, based in the village, produces a vatted malt whisky called Poit Dhubh and two blends. It does not describe a whisky still on Skye. The Isle of Skye article says the blended whisky branded Isle of Skye is made at Glengoyne, not on the island.
rows.reject_reason: Pràban na Linne vat and blend whisky at Isleornsay. The page does not place a whisky still on Skye. Poit Dhubh is the name of a vatted malt, not a still the article locates on the island.
rows.summary: Pràban na Linne, founded by Iain Noble and based at Isleornsay on Skye, produces a vatted malt whisky called Poit Dhubh and the blends Tè Bheag nan Eilean and Mac na Mara. Vatting and blending are not a still on the island. The blended whisky branded Isle of Skye is made at Glengoyne, not on Skye.

rows.title: Mock whisky plant at Colbost
rows.evidence: The Colbost article says a hut in the museum garden contains a mock illegal whisky brewing plant. It does not say a still worked at Colbost. Skye's illicit stills are already filed from the Talisker article.
rows.reject_reason: The page describes a mock illegal whisky plant in a museum hut at Colbost, not a still that worked on Skye.
rows.summary: At Colbost on Skye, a hut in the museum garden contains a mock illegal whisky brewing plant. The article calls it a mock, and it does not place a working or historical still in the village.

rows.title: Eday peat for mainland distilleries
rows.evidence: The Eday article says peat from Eday was exported to whisky distilleries on mainland Scotland. It does not place a still on Eday.
rows.reject_reason: Eday supplied peat to whisky distilleries on mainland Scotland. The page does not place a still on the island.
rows.summary: Peat extraction was an important industry on Eday. Sanday and North Ronaldsay took fuel from the island, and peat was also exported to whisky distilleries on mainland Scotland. The stills were on the mainland, not on Eday.

rows.title: The Cairnsmuir
rows.evidence: The Tiree article says that in 2020 the company was marketing a Speyside whisky, The Cairnsmuir, but not made on Tiree.
rows.reject_reason: The page says The Cairnsmuir is a Speyside whisky and was not made on Tiree.
rows.summary: In 2020 the Tiree company was marketing a Speyside whisky called The Cairnsmuir. The article says it was not made on Tiree. The still is not on the island.
